newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut not yet decided on $400 mln eurobond--Bank.
newsitem.headline: Beirut not yet decided on $400 mln eurobond--Bank.

text.p: Lebanon has not yet decided on a new $400 million eurobond issue in 1997 as reported earlier in the press, central bank governor Riad Salameh said on Thursday.

"Contrary to the information in the press, the government has not yet taken the decision to issue eurobonds for $400 million in 1997," Salameh said in remarks published by the French language daily L'Orient-Le Jour.

Bank of Lebanon vice governor Nasser Saidi was quoted by an-Nahar daily on Monday as saying Lebanon would issue a $400 million eurobond in October 1997 to cover its trail-blazing three-year $400-million bond which matures that month.
Salameh's office confirmed his remarks, in which he added: "It is probably a confusion, since on October 14 (1997) Lebanon has to reimburse $400 million borrowed three years ago."
The government, which has so far received parliamentary authorisation to accumulate $900 million foreign debt, will need new parliamentary approval for further eurobond issues.

It has so far issued eurobonds worth $800 million -- a $400 million three-year issue in September 1994, a four-year $300 million issue in July 1995 and a $100 million addition to the four-year issue last May.
Information Minister Farid Makari said last month the finance ministry was preparing a $100 million eurobond for the state-run electricity utility.
